### Given Data:
- Mass of solute ($	ext{NaOH}$), $W = 40\text{ g}$
- Volume of solution, $V = 2000\text{ mL} = 2.0\text{ L}$
- Chemical formula of caustic soda = $	ext{NaOH}$

### Step 1: Calculate the Gram Equivalent Mass of $	ext{NaOH}$
- Molecular weight of $	ext{NaOH} = (23 \times 1) + (16 \times 1) + (1 \times 1) = 40\text{ g/mol}$
- Acidity/Basicity ($	ext{n-factor}$) of $	ext{NaOH} = 1$ (since it releases one $	ext{OH}^-$ ion per molecule).
- $\text{Equivalent Weight} = \frac{\text{Molecular Weight}}{\text{n-factor}} = \frac{40}{1} = 40\text{ g/eq}$

### Step 2: Calculate Normality ($N$)
$$\text{Normality } (N) = \frac{\text{Number of gram equivalents}}{\text{Volume of solution in liters}}$$
$$\text{Number of gram equivalents} = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Equivalent Weight}} = \frac{40\text{ g}}{40\text{ g/eq}} = 1\text{ eq}$$
$$\text{Normality } (N) = \frac{1\text{ eq}}{2.0\text{ L}} = 0.5\text{ N}$$

**Answer:** The Normality of the solution is **$0.5\text{ N}$**.
proTip: Always state the n-factor clearly when calculating equivalent weight for base or acid problems.
